candidate: D - buy size back by fixing execution and carry
one_line: Fixing the entry to rest as a real maker buys 1.40x authorised size (paired-seed, 12/12 seeds, t=63) and is a cheap, safe, executor-only change - but the authorised-size number it multiplies collapses to zero under ANY perturbation of the input data series, so it must ship as a cost reduction, not as a size authorisation.

measured_on.window: 2024-07 -> 2026-07 (the single-touch holdout; also the only window where perp/spot basis data exists)
measured_on.basis: PERP space, net of funding - NOT the spot basis every published number in this repo uses
measured_on.note: bars_4h_btcusd.csv already carries ~2515 prior trials per RESEARCH_PROTOCOL; every number here is an upper bound on honest size and none of it is a forecast.

size_multiple.break_even_note: exact and analytic: a worse fill price and a higher fee enter the P&L through the SAME term, so there is no Kelly nonlinearity to discover. The sweep confirms it - at a 2.88 bps penalty rec_m returns to 0.43, identical to doing nothing.

new_measurement_the_basis.what: Hyperliquid BTC perp close vs Bitstamp spot close, 4612 aligned 4h bars, 2024-06-17 -> 2026-07-25. Never measured in this repo before.
new_measurement_the_basis.why_it_matters: 70% of bars carry a basis larger than 2.88 bps - the ENTIRE prize from fixing the fee. The mis-pricing the fix corrects is smaller than the noise it sits in.
new_measurement_the_basis.is_it_removable: NO. Signalling on perp bars to eliminate it destroys the edge (rec_m 0.47 -> 0.00). The basis drag must be accepted, not engineered away.

alo_rejection_mechanism.root_cause_quoted_from_code: mirror.py:4486 - 'The engine prices signals off SPOT but we trade a FUTURE; at a positive basis short limits are marketable and post-only is rejected.'
alo_rejection_mechanism.confirmed: engine bars are Bitstamp/Kraken spot (app/sources/bitstamp.py); /exec/target publishes pend.limit = the raw spot bar close (main.py:103); the venue is the HL perp.
alo_rejection_mechanism.UNEXPLAINED: The basis+latency model does NOT explain 4 of 4 rejections (p=0.019). Something else is acting and I will not guess it - see open questions.
alo_rejection_mechanism.latency_chain: paper engine POLL_SECONDS=60 (render.yaml) + executor poll_seconds=20 (config.py:76) = up to 80s from bar close to the venue
alo_rejection_mechanism.basis_translation_is_NOT_the_fix: translating the limit to the perp's own last price leaves a ~49% cross rate (bid-ask bounce plus drift) - WORSE than today's 32%. The order must rest on the PASSIVE side of the perp spread, not at its last price.

funding_at_size.headline: Funding does NOT constrain the $1m target. It is a proportional haircut, not a ceiling - it scales with notional exactly like fees, so the ratio at $1m is identical to the ratio at $15k.
funding_at_size.first_measurement_of_the_trend_leg: phase 1 measured the pullback leg only and refused to guess the trend leg. Both are measured here.
funding_at_size.REGIME_WARNING: The same book pays 5.66%/yr of gross in 2023 and EARNS 0.40% in 2026. A 14x swing with the window. Phase 1's +0.0202%/yr credit, my -0.13% and my -1.86% are three different windows of the same quantity and all three are correct. Funding is NOT a constant to quote.
funding_at_size.why_the_book_pays_despite_being_half_sho: the book is long-biased exactly when funding is hot (phase 1 found 62% long in hot regimes on the pullback leg). The two halves do not cancel over the full history - they only cancelled in the cool 2025-26 window phase 1 happened to measure.

THE_BLOCKER.what: authorised size survives only on the exact price AND volume series the strategy was selected on
THE_BLOCKER.sample_size_is_controlled: the spot_price+PERP_volume cell holds n at 145 against the live 148 and STILL zeroes the p10, so this is not a small-n artifact
THE_BLOCKER.kill_rule: kelly.py kills at prob_negative_edge > 0.25. The perp/perp cell is at 0.343 - KILLED by the repo's own rule.
THE_BLOCKER.reading: The price conditions transfer at 94% - the same as the pure-price donchian control. The volume filter drops agreement to 69%, and removing it takes rec_m from 0.47 to 0.00 on spot bars. The measured edge is concentrated in the single most venue-specific input the strategy reads.
THE_BLOCKER.consequence: The 1.40x is a real multiple on a number that is not robust. Multiplying a fragile base by 1.40 does not make it less fragile.

does_it_reach_1m.note: FIX 1 roughly halves the equity needed for $1m against phase 1's today-figure, but $1m on $100k equity is 10x gross/equity against a measured authorised 0.65-0.93x. Candidate D is an edge lever; it cannot substitute for capital.
does_it_reach_1m.rail_still_binds_first: every arm measured, INCLUDING the un-fixed baseline at $64,535, exceeds MAX_NOTIONAL_USD $20,000. The fee fix cannot move one dollar of live size until the rail moves.

code_change.separation_of_powers: the change lives ENTIRELY in the credentialed executor. The engine stays a keyless decision brain and keeps publishing the spot limit unchanged - it must not read the venue book, which is precisely why the re-pricing cannot live there.
code_change.unbooked_fill_unprotected_interaction: a true maker fill lands LATER inside the bar than a crossing fill, so the window between fill and the engine's next bar-close booking gets SHORTER on average. The change does not create a new unprotected window and does not remove the existing structural one.
code_change.net_mirror_invariants: the retry stays INSIDE place_limit under the SAME cloid, exactly as the existing Gtc retry already does, so the mirror still sees one cloid and one order and its identity/dedupe machinery (mirror.py L2600-2660) is untouched. Any non-post-only error still raises, as today.
code_change.new_operational_cost: up to ~1s of extra wall clock inside place_limit before the mirror's _ostat(cloid) read, which can turn a CONFIRMED read into UNKNOWN. That is the SAFE direction - UNKNOWN is treated as possibly-live and the ref is kept - so the failure mode is a spurious entry_unconfirmed RED page, not a lost or duplicated order.
code_change.second_order_divergence: the engine computes the stop from ITS limit (stop = limit +/- 2.5*ATR) and the mirror places that level regardless of our fill, so a re-priced fill carries a stop off by the fill offset: ~10 bps against a 414 bps median stop distance, i.e. ~2.4% of intended risk.

open_questions_ranked: P1 - The live pending limits and FILL PRICES for the 4 observed Alo crossings. My basis+latency model predicts a 32-39% cross rate and 4/4 is p=0.019, so a mechanism I cannot see is acting. It decides whether the fix is the ~15-line re-price proposed here or something upstream. The executor records cloids in hl.post_only_crosses and _watch_fill captures fill prices, so the order log may already hold it. I will not guess it.

P1 - Is the volume filter's contribution understood and intended? Removing it takes rec_m 0.47 -> 0.00, and it is the single most venue-specific input the strategy reads (volume series correlate 0.61 across venues vs 0.999 for prices). This is a strategy-design decision for Casey, not a research output, and it gates any size increase.
P1 - cash_apy on the ~$100k spot USDC. Inherited from phase 1, still unanswered. RESEARCH_FEES.md measured this one dimension moving S5's m from 0.30 to 0.79 - larger than everything in this study.
P2 - Which fee basis is the registered objective (engine default 12.00 bps vs measured 8.64)? It moves rec_m ~5x and commit 132e0a6 says re-registering it is a dated protocol amendment Casey signs.

P2 - Which window governs? All my basis-adjusted numbers are necessarily on 2024-07 -> 2026-07 because that is where perp candles reach. That is also the conservative holdout, so I defer to it - but it is a protocol call.
P3 - Is Casey adding capital? $1m of gross needs ~$1.07m of equity even after FIX 1. The deposit plan, not the edge, decides the $1m question.
